claims.claim: Semantic HTML uses element names whose defined meanings describe the role of content rather than merely acting as generic containers.
The main element represents the dominant content of a document's body and a document must not have more than one main element without a hierarchy attribute.
An article is a self-contained composition that could in principle be independently distributed or reused, while a section is a thematic grouping and not a generic styling container.
A nav element identifies a major navigation block; not every cluster of links needs nav markup.
Native HTML landmark elements provide landmark semantics, and labeling distinguishable landmarks is useful when more than one exists.
A header or footer describes the nearest sectioning content or sectioning root, rather than always the whole page.
